pr_title: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert

comments.comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

pr_title: feat(upsampling) - Support upsampled error count with performance optimizations

comments.comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check 'if client_sample_rate:' treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python's built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won't match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them.
The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. Upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing
OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation

pr_title: Span Buffer Multiprocess Enhancement with Health Monitoring

comments.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' and 'shards' for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won't actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above.
Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown.

The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.
to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs, JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer.

comments.comment: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods. This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey.
Wrong value 6 passed for group_2 occurrence — the data packet specifies 'group_2': 10. Should be 10 to accurately reflect the test scenario.
